cases.claim: Identical marginals do not identify joint group coverage
Same marginal predictions can reverse the optimal two-item batch
Static expected coverage stays submodular under an arbitrary fixed joint law
Static submodularity does not imply adaptive submodularity: a positive in one group raises another group's conditional gain
Primary-hit-only observations do not identify full-library outcomes
One selected item per group makes D equal H without a second independent achievement
A one-per-group quota can lose expected positive-group coverage to classical probability-aware selection
A classical hit/coverage tradeoff exists with independent labels
Preference weights change the chosen portfolio; a toy weight is not an owner-approved material-effect criterion
Correcting primary-to-confirmation calibration can change ranking without creating a new optimizer
Known-group binary confirmation coverage embeds in a multiclass diminishing-returns utility
Feedback can have value under a known joint model; this does not distinguish the mechanism from Bayesian active search

interpretation: Exact illustrative mechanism checks, not empirical utility, novelty proof or a new algorithm evaluation
